newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Sears sees record holiday sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Sears sees record holiday sales.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co is expecting record holiday sales, keyed by strong results in many types of merchandise including apparel and tools, said John Costello, senior executive vice president of marketing.
"We expect sales to top last year, and produce a record holiday season," Costello told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Costello said sales have met company internal plans through the weekend, ended December 8.
Chairman Arthur Martinez said in an interview in late November that he expects same-store retail sales to be up about six percent from a year ago.
"Sales gains were broadly based throughout the store and by geographic region (across the United States)," Costello said.
Apparel was performing quite well across a wide range of categories, and the company's hard goods such as Craftsman tools, computers, and seasonal items were also selling well.
Despite a lagging consumer electronics retailing sector, Costello said Sears has posted increases in electronics sales versus a year ago, with computers leading the way.

Costello said the seven-day period, beginning December 14, will be a "solid week" for items such as televisions and stereos, since they are "thoughtful purchases, and it's too early for electronics purchases at this stage."

Sears launched the advertising theme, "Come See the Merry Side of Sears" last year, and is continuing the marketing strategy through high-profile television sponsorships with radio and newspaper support.
"Generating broad-scale awareness is an important part of our strategy," Costello said.
Industry sources estimated that Sears holiday marketing spending totaled more than $1.2 billion in 1995, and Sears is expected to spend about the same this year, despite a shorter holiday season.
The $1.2 billion in spending includes newspapers, television, and radio advertising.
Costello also said that the $4 billion, five-year store remodeling program, which started in 1993, has also helped improve results.
The remodeling program converted more "backroom space into selling space" and allowed the company to offer a broader variety of merchandise.
In 1995, Sears fourth-quarter sales accounted for $10.9 billion of its annual $34.9 billion sales, and $455 million of its $1.8 billion in net income.

Fourth quarter profits were expected to be about the same proportion of total net income for 1996, as the proportion of profits for the fourth quarter were compared to the full year of 1995, Costello said.
